Compute Normalized Moran's \(I\)

normalized.moran.Rd

A simple function to compute the normalized "\(I_6\)" Moran's \(I\) statistic proposed by Tillé et al. (2026), called by normalized.moran.test and normalized.moran.mc.

Usage

normalized.moran(
  x,
  listw,
  zero.policy = attr(listw, "zero.policy"),
  NAOK = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector the same length as the neighbours list in listw

listw

a listw object of style 'W' created for example by nb2listw

zero.policy

default attr(listw, "zero.policy") as set when listw was created, if attribute not set, use global option value; if TRUE assign zero to the lagged value of zones without neighbours, if FALSE assign NA

NAOK

if 'TRUE' then any 'NA' or 'NaN' or 'Inf' values in x are passed on to the foreign function. If 'FALSE', the presence of 'NA' or 'NaN' or 'Inf' values is regarded as an error.

Value

The normalized "\(I_6\)" Moran's \(I\) of the values in x is computed, as a numeric vector of length one.

Author

Diego Giuliani diego.giuliani@unitn.it

References

Tillé Y., Giuliani D., Dickson M.M., Espa G. (2026) Revisiting the Normalization of the Moran's \(I\) index: A Correlation-based Approach with Inference, International Statistical Review

See also

normalized.moran.test, normalized.moran.mc

Examples

library(spdep)
data(oldcol)
col.W <- nb2listw(COL.nb, style="W")
crime <- COL.OLD$CRIME
normalized.moran(crime, col.W)
#> [1] 0.6908337
is.na(crime) <- sample(1:length(crime), 10)
normalized.moran(crime, col.W, NAOK=TRUE)
#> Warning: NAs in lagged values
#> [1] 0.449429
